intervention: double share of vegetarian options from 25% to 50%
effect_size: +7.8 percentage points vegetarian sales (+40.8%) experimental; +14.9 and +14.5 pp (+61.8%, +78.8%) observational
outcome_measure: share of meals sold that were vegetarian
follow_up: same-day; checked other mealtimes, no rebound found
notes: Little effect on total sales; biggest effect among diners who rarely chose vegetarian

intervention: raise meat-free options from one in three to two in three
effect_size: -19.9 percentage points share of meat meals (95% CI -25.2 to -14.6)
follow_up: weeks; no change in other cafeterias
notes: Study 2 in 18 worksite cafeterias: +2.3 pp, not robust, poor implementation

intervention: vegetarian lunch as the default at registration
notes: Men more likely to opt out; excluded from the Green 2025 meta-analysis for lack of delayed outcome

intervention: plant-based meal as the default on RSVP form
effect_size: risk ratio 3.52 (95% CI 2.44 to 5.09) of choosing plant-based meal

intervention: Veganuary multi-component in-store promotion (visibility, availability, price, placement)
effect_size: plant-based unit sales +57% during (IRR 1.56), +15% after (IRR 1.14); no significant change in meat sales
study_design: natural experiment with pre and post periods

intervention: placement, taste and social-norm nudges for meat and dairy alternatives
effect_size: alternatives +10% (IRR 1.10, 95% CI 0.99 to 1.23, not significant); meat -3% (not significant)

intervention: 10% temporary price reduction on plant-based beef, alone or with feature advert
effect_size: +20% units with discount alone; +80% with discount plus feature
study_design: econometric price and promotion model on store scanner data
notes: Promotional efficiency of the category is low because promotions are frequent

intervention: price parity for private-label vegan range (Vemondo)
effect_size: vegan sales +30% or more in six months (company claim)
notes: Whole German plant-based meat market volume +6.2% in 2024 then -1.7% in 2025 (GLB-09; GLB-08); meat sales effect not reported

intervention: sector protein targets plus price parity pledges by several retailers
outcome_measure: plant share of all protein sold
notes: Plant-based meat volume fell 6.2% (2024) and 10.7% (2025) over the same period

intervention: prominent advertising of a new plant-based burger (Impossible)
effect_size: purchase-probability lift for meat-burger buyers about one fifth of that for vegan-burger buyers
study_design: ad exposure data merged with household scanner panel
notes: Advertising mainly recruited existing vegan-burger buyers

intervention: all meat-reduction interventions with at least one day follow-up (meta-analysis)
effect_size: pooled SMD 0.07 (95% CI 0.02 to 0.12); red and processed meat only 0.25; choice architecture 0.21 (3 estimates); 0.2 if weaker designs included
notes: Most vegetarian-default studies lacked delayed outcomes and were excluded; North American effect 0.04

intervention: weekly vegetarian meal mandated in school canteens
effect_size: effect on total meat intake not measured in retrieved sources
notes: Policy precedent only; retrieved studies address nutrition, emissions and children's liking
